block.paragraph: This calculation determines longitudinal thermal movement of the two-span FIB 36 pedestrian bridge for joint and bearing detailing. The two simple spans are treated as one continuous deck unit with the center of movement at the intermediate pier. Geometry is referenced live from Bridge Geometry_2 Beam.

textcell.name: MovementScope1
textcell.paragraph: • Concrete-only superstructure temperature range is taken from FDOT SDG Table 2.7.1-1 .

textcell.name: MovementScope2
textcell.paragraph: • Center of movement is assumed at the intermediate pier; each end movement therefore uses the adjacent span length.

textcell.name: MovementScope3
textcell.paragraph: • This module calculates thermal movement only. Creep, shrinkage, skew resolution, and final expansion-joint or bearing capacity checks are separate design items.

block.paragraph: Reference packet: C003 highlighted code references . Edition basis: FDOT Structures Manual I.6.B.5 .
• FDOT SDG 2.7.1 : Concrete Only temperature range = 70°F mean, 105°F high, 35°F low.
• FDOT SDG 6.3 : Calculate bridge movement about an assumed 70°F construction mean and base joint/bearing design on the SDG Table 2.7.1-1 temperature range.
• FDOT SDG 2.7.1.D : Temperature rise and fall load effects use 120% of the tabulated maximum temperature change in accordance with LRFD Table 3.4.1-1 .
Related factor provisions: LRFD Table 3.4.1-6 and LRFD C3.4.1 . See the packet’s QC qualification on the unfactored joint/bearing label.
• LRFD 5.4.2.2 : Normal-weight concrete coefficient of thermal expansion is taken as 6.0×10⁻⁶ /°F.

For uniform temperature change, longitudinal movement is calculated from δ = α·ΔT·L. Temperature rise moves each end away from the intermediate pier; temperature fall moves each end toward the pier. For an end joint referenced to the approach, these correspond respectively to joint closing and opening.
Supplemental equation context: LRFD Eq. 3.12.2.3-1 gives the full high-to-low thermal movement range; C003 calculates excursions from the mean.

No joint or bearing adequacy conclusion is made in this module because allowable movement depends on the selected joint/bearing system and, for expansion-joint design, the applicable creep, shrinkage, skew, and other movement components.
